## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
#Step 3.3: Visualize the ancestry of one sample and one chromosome
#For a chromosome chrII of sample A01_62, create a figure where the x axis is the position and colors indicate whether the genotype was a 0 or a 1. Make sure to convert the genotype to a factor variable.
setwd("~/qb25-answers/week3")

gtlong_df <- read.table("gt_long.txt", header = TRUE)

A0162_chr2 <- gtlong_df%>%
  filter(Sample_ID == "A01_62") %>%
    filter(Chromosome == "chrII")

A0162_chr2_fig <- ggplot(A0162_chr2, aes(x=Position, y=Sample_ID, color = as.factor(Genotype)))+
  geom_point()

ggsave(plot = A0162_chr2_fig, path = "~/qb25-answers/week3", filename = "A0162_chr2_fig.png")

#Question 3.2: Do you notice any patterns? What do the transitions indicate?
#the ends of the chromosome we inherited from the wine strain, as they fell under "1". While there is a chunk in the middle of chr II that is inherited from the lab strain (0). This means there was a recombination event, with breakpoints appearing where the genotype switches from one parental strain to the other. 

```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
#Step 3.4: Expand your visualization
#Now use facet_grid to plot all chromosomes for sample A01_62. Use the scales = "free_x" and space = "free_x" options to allow for different x-axis scales for different chromosomes. Extend your plot to consider all samples. Note that different samples do not need their own facets, but can simply be arranged along the y axis (which can accept variables that are not numeric!).

A0162 <- gtlong_df%>%
  filter(Sample_ID == "A01_62")

A0162_fig <- ggplot(A0162, aes(x=Position, y=Sample_ID, color = as.factor(Genotype))) +
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(. ~ Chromosome, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

gtlong_fig <- ggplot(gtlong_df, aes(x=Position, y=Sample_ID, color = as.factor(Genotype))) +
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(. ~ Chromosome, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

ggsave(plot = gtlong_fig, path = "~/qb25-answers/week3", filename = "gtlong_fig.png")

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
